name.description: Optional short handle for the session ([a-z0-9-], ≤24), e.g. "cli-cleanup". Linked sessions and plan steps refer to it by this name; derived from the title when omitted.

use_worktree.description: "fresh" only (rejected with "fork"). false = shares this session's checkout and can edit it (in a worktree session: its worktree, branch and PR, so never for work that ends in a branch or PR of its own or belongs in another repository); not accepted from a session set up to move from the user's checkout into a worktree with EnterWorktree (before or after it moves), one working in a worktree on an SSH host, or one whose worktree was given back. target.description: "fresh" only. "local" (default) = where this session runs. "cloud" = run it as a cloud session (keeps going when this computer sleeps). host.description: With target "ssh": the name of one of the user's saved SSH connections (as list_start_targets reports it) — never a raw hostname, user or key. The app connects as the user configured it and may ask them to sign in.

cwd.description: The folder the session works in, when it is not this project: an absolute (or ~/) path on the host it will run on — this computer, this session's host, or the SSH connection named by host (default there: the connection's folder). Must exist; if the user has not trusted it yet the app asks them first. "fresh" only.

environment.description: With target "cloud": the name or id of one of the user's cloud environments (list_start_targets lists them); omitted = the default one. Default in this project: this session's base branch (the one picked when it started, or the one its worktree was cut from). If the session has none and either it runs on an SSH host or its project folder is itself a git worktree or submodule, the folder's current commit. Only for a session that gets its own worktree (use_worktree true, or the place's default); not with target "cloud".

preset.description: The name of one of the user's saved session presets on this computer: it names the place itself (a folder here or an SSH connection and folder — do not pass host or cwd with it) and brings model, effort and worktree defaults plus its saved environment variables; use_worktree/model/effort override those. effort.description: "fresh" only, optional: reasoning effort at or below yours. Omit to inherit.

permission_mode.description: Optional, local starts only: the permission mode it starts in — this session's own or a lower one (omit to inherit it). A higher mode, or one the app does not offer here, is refused; raising a session is set_session_permission_mode's card to show.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan
tools.description:
Keep the task list the app shows under your latest message while you work: the user follows your progress by it and will never ask for it, so it is part of the task. Every request that edits files or runs more than one command gets one (implement-and-test, investigate-then-fix, anything the user listed); only a single-command answer or pure conversation does not.

Never spend a message on this tool alone: send it IN THE SAME MESSAGE as another tool call (in parallel), so it costs no extra round trip.
- First call: with the VERY FIRST tool call of the turn, even one that only reads or lists files: {"items": [...]}, the whole plan in order, short imperative phrases (at most ~7 words, no numbering), the step you are starting "in_progress", the rest "pending". If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the list once you know.
- Next step: {"advance": true} alongside the call that begins it (completes the in_progress step, starts the next pending one); after the last step, advance alongside wrap_up.
- Out of order: {"done": [2], "start": 4} (1-based).
- Plan changed, including right after the user interrupts or sends a new instruction mid-task: {"items": [...]} again, the new whole list, so the pinned list never shows an abandoned plan.
- Every {"items"} call says in "scope" what this request is to the session: "first_task" (nothing finished here yet); after that, "new_task" (unrelated work: it builds on nothing done, found or decided here) or "continuation" (everything else: anything a few tool calls settle, the next iteration, acting on what you just investigated or suggested, even if that work gets its own commit or PR; when unsure, this one). A "new_task" turn opens with a start_session offer and reaches this call only if the user chose Do it here.
Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: propose it and call this.

The result says which case below applies. When the box shows your question, it ends your turn: write no text after this call, since the recap and question say what the user needs and your work above holds the detail. Otherwise your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, with any question the box did not show.

Fields — recap and ask are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label and message are the user's words back to you:
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

# Commit Hook Performance Analysis

> **Historical.** This analysis predates the removal of shadow branches: turn ends now record pending work in session state only, so the shadow-branch resolution, ref scans, and tree reads measured below no longer exist on the commit hook path. The numbers are kept for context; re-measure before relying on them.

## Test Results (2026-02-27)

Measured on a full-history single-branch clone of `entireio/cli` with 200 seeded branches and packed refs.
Each session generated with a unique base commit from repo history. ENDED sessions are split 75/25
between shadow-branch sessions (expensive path) and committed sessions (cheap path), matching
production distribution observed in `.git/entire-sessions/`.

| Scenario | Sessions | Control | Prepare | PostCommit | Total | Overhead |
|----------|----------|---------|---------|------------|-------|----------|
| 100      | 100      | 29ms    | 815ms   | 6.491s     | 7.306s | 7.276s  |
| 200      | 200      | 20ms    | 1.651s  | 14.629s    | 16.28s | 16.26s  |
| 500      | 500      | 29ms    | 4.433s  | 46.934s    | 51.37s | 51.34s  |

**Scaling: ~73ms per session at 100, ~81ms at 200, ~103ms at 500.** PostCommit dominates overwhelmingly.
Control commit (no Entire) is ~25-30ms regardless of session count.

The 200-session result (**16.28s**) closely matches the real-world user report of **~16s for ~95 sessions**,
confirming the test methodology now faithfully reproduces production overhead.

### Session distribution per scenario

| Scenario | ENDED (shadow) | ENDED (committed) | IDLE | ACTIVE |
|----------|---------------|-------------------|------|--------|
| 100      | 66            | 22                | 11   | 1      |
| 200      | 132           | 44                | 22   | 2      |
| 500      | 330           | 110               | 55   | 5      |

### Impact of test methodology

This test went through several iterations to achieve realistic numbers:

| Version | 100 sess | 200 sess | 500 sess | Per-session | Issue |
|---------|----------|----------|----------|-------------|-------|
| Shallow + shared base | 1.74s | 3.59s | 9.52s | ~18ms | Packfile too small, repeated ref scan |
| Full history + shared base | 2.00s | 4.16s | 10.9s | ~21ms | Same ref scanned N times |
| Full history + unique bases (cheap ENDED) | 337ms | 617ms | 1.52s | ~3ms | ENDED sessions had LastCheckpointID → no-ops |
| **Full history + realistic ENDED (current)** | **7.3s** | **16.3s** | **51.4s** | **~73-103ms** | **Matches production** |

The critical fix was making ENDED sessions realistic: 75% have shadow branches with data but **no** `LastCheckpointID`.
These exercise the full expensive path: ref resolution → commit/tree resolution → transcript/overlap checking →
condensation during PostCommit. Previously, all ENDED sessions had `LastCheckpointID` set, making them trivial no-ops
that skipped the entire hot path.

## How go-git `repo.Reference()` works

go-git has **no caching** for packed ref lookups. Each `repo.Reference()` call:
1. Tries to read a loose ref file (`.git/refs/heads/<name>`)
2. On miss, opens `packed-refs` and scans line-by-line until match or EOF
3. For refs that don't exist, scans the **entire** file every time

After `git pack-refs --all` (the default state after `git gc`), all refs are in packed-refs and loose ref files don't exist. This means every lookup scans the file.

## Scaling Dimensions

### 1. PostCommit condensation — the dominant cost (~50-80ms/session)

When PostCommit processes an ENDED session with new content (shadow branch exists, no `LastCheckpointID`),
it triggers the full condensation pipeline:

1. **Ref resolution**: `repo.Reference()` to find shadow branch (~1ms)

One change is worth making: every `git commit --amend` now runs a `git config` subprocess, even when there's no session and no trailer. The rest are small or rare. Here, 20 runs of `git config --get-regexp` took about 3 ms of CPU each (wall time was inflated by the sandbox), so call it 2–5 ms per spawn. Post-commit never spawns.

**`git config` spawns per hook invocation (prepare-commit-msg / commit-msg):**

| Commit shape | prepare | commit-msg |
|---|---|---|
| Editor commit, a session has content | 1 | 1 |
| Editor commit, no session or no content | 0 | 0 |
| `-m` / `-F` (agents' usual path) | 0 | 0 (the last-line check skips it) |
| Amend (source "commit") | 1, always | 1 with editor, 0 with `--no-edit` |
| Squash with SQUASH_MSG, editor | 2 (inherit, then main path) | 1 |
| Redo, editor | 2 | 1 |
| Squash + redo | 3 | 1 |
| Amend + redo | 2 | 1 |
| Agent fast path | 0 with `-m`, 1 with editor source | as above |

**Findings:**

1. **`cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_hooks.go:827` (handleAmendCommitMsg).** `gitCommentPrefix` runs on every amend, before any session or trailer check. That adds one spawn (2–5 ms) to every amend in an enabled repo.
   - Cheaper: compute `mentioned := trailers.ParseAllCheckpoints(message)` first. If it's empty, skip the spawn and both deleted-list checks. This is safe because every ID the final-block parser accepts also matches that regex.
   - **Worth changing.**

2. **Squash and redo read the same config twice.** Squash calls it at `:709` and again at `:533`; redo calls it at `manual_commit_redo.go:135` and again at `:533`. The value doesn't change within a hook, and for `auto` the inserted trailers sit above git's comment block, so the answer stays valid.
   - Cheaper: cache the raw config value once per process (`sync.OnceValue`, or a cwd-keyed cache like `hooksDirCache` in `strategy/hooks.go:70`) and resolve `auto` per message. Saves 1–2 spawns on these rare shapes.
   - **Worth it, low priority.**

3. **`manual_commit_hooks.go:2762` (addTrailerForAgentCommit).** The prefix is only used by `stampedTrailer`; the trailer is added with `addCheckpointTrailer`, which doesn't need it.
   - Cheaper: guard with `strings.Contains(message, trailers.CheckpointTrailerKey)`, or make the prefix lazy so `stampedTrailer` asks only when an ID is present. Saves 1 spawn on editor-source fast-path commits (for example a human with `commit_linking=always`).
   - **Worth it; trivial.**

4. **`manual_commit_hooks.go:206` (CommitMsg).** This spawn is needed for the editor shape.
   - Cheaper: read the prefix back from the sentinel comment line prepare-commit-msg wrote ("<prefix> Remove the Entire-Checkpoint trailer above…"), falling back to the spawn.
   - **Not worth it:** it couples the two hooks, and the user has just spent seconds in the editor.

5. **`:827` / `:834`, `withoutDeletedCheckpoints` called twice.** Each call reads and JSON-parses the deleted-checkpoints file (`gitdir.CommonDir` is cached, so no spawn). `stripDeletedCheckpointTrailers` at `:445` already loaded the same file. The second load happens only when the final block has IDs and all of them are deleted, which the earlier strip makes nearly impossible. Cost is under 0.1 ms.
   - Cheaper: load the set once per hook and pass it down (the pattern predates this PR).
   - **Not worth it in this PR.**

6. **Repeated splitting of the same message.**
   - `StripEditorComments` (`trailers.go:189`) splits and joins in `CutAtScissors`, then splits and joins again; `finalTrailerBlock` splits a third time.
   - CommitMsg splits the whole message twice via `lastNonBlankLine` (`:332`), plus `CutAtScissors`.
   - `isScissorsLine` (`trailers.go:180`) builds `prefix+" "+marker` on every call, and `AutoCommentPrefix` calls it for 10 candidates per line.
   - With `commit -v` the file holds the whole diff, so the full splits grow with diff size: microseconds normally, about 1 ms for huge diffs.
   - Cheaper: build the scissors string once outside the loop, and scan backwards for the last non-blank line.
   - **Nit, not worth it.**

7. **go-git config instead of the subprocess.** go-git v6 beta.1 exposes `cfg.Core.CommentChar` (`config/config.go:545`), and `commentString` is readable via `Raw`; the repo is already open on the main prepare path.
   - It doesn't handle `include`/`includeIf`, `GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS` (so `git -c core.commentChar=…` passed to hooks would be lost), or `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT`.
   - It also can't tell which of `commentChar`/`commentString` was set last across config files, which git relies on to pick the prefix.
   - CommitMsg has no open repo.
   - It would save 2–4 ms, but a wrong prefix loses the trailer or keeps a comment.
   - **Not worth it.** There's precedent for shelling out on hook paths: `strategy/checkpoint_sync_capture.go:254`.
